publication: Spencer Unger, Forcing Summer School Lecture Notes, UCLA Logic Summer School2014, last modified2014-09-06;44-page PDF, printed p.=PDF p. Sections10.1–10.2 written by Justin Palumbo; section10.3 by Sherwood Hachtman, based on Richard Laver lectures.

reviews.checked_passages: Section10.1 pp.26–30 (generic filters, names, evaluation, rank and structural properties); section10.2 pp.31–33 (semantic forcing and extension axiom proofs); section10.3 pp.34–36 (auxiliary forcing-star recursion, truth lemma and semantic forcing definability).
reviews.consumers: [Forcing orders and generic filters](entries/forcing-and-generic-filters/entry.html), [Names and generic extensions](entries/forcing-names/entry.html), [The forcing theorem](entries/forcing-theorem/entry.html); [ZFC in generic extensions](entries/forcing-extensions/entry.html).
reviews.outcome: UNGER-FORCING-01 records the incomplete Union witness proof and its explicit refinement repair. Names use exact least rank sup(child-rank+1), and the binary example on p.31 is read with p(2) in {0,1}, not the printed2. Forcing-star is an auxiliary relation, not semantic forcing: double-negation translation supplies the latter. Definability is a separate scheme for each fixed formula, with no global class truth predicate. Replacement and Power Set first produce bounding sets and use established Separation for exact sets; Collection needs its least-witness-rank derivation from Replacement. Sections11–12, iterations, CH consistency and symmetric models are not audited/adopted here.

reviews.checked_passages: Adoption reuses the previously assessed section10.1 generic-filter and descending-refinement foundations. The arbitrary-order, countable-family extension is an explicit corpus derivation from these foundations and Choice, not a newly certified source theorem.
reviews.outcome: One selector is chosen for all requirement/condition pairs before natural-number recursion. Its exact descending sequence generates the stated filter, with maximum indices supplying directedness. At most countable families include the empty family, handled by a principal filter. No countability assumption on the order and no chain condition are used; the earlier least-index countable-order proof remains available. No source-audit expansion or new defect claim.
